candidates.attacker_control: The 'changenote' parameter of an edit POST to Edit.jsp (findParam -> request.getParameter) plus the standard 'ok'/'text'/'spamhash' fields (and the spam-filter hidden field value rendered by the editor) submitted by any user allowed to edit or comment.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that no downstream encoding exists on the save/read path (DefaultPageManager.putPageText simply delegates; VersioningFileProvider stores and returns the attribute verbatim; JSP EL ${...} performs no HTML escaping; WikiJSPFilter only injects resources). Confirmed the intended pattern exists for the same field elsewhere: Comment.jsp:86 and AttachmentServlet:518-522 call TextUtil.replaceEntities() before storing, and replaceEntities() escapes &, <, > and " (TextUtil.java:211-218), which would neutralize the payload; only Edit.jsp omits it. RecentChangesPlugin/RSS render change notes through JDOM/XML which escapes them, so the Info tab/editor templates are the exploitable sinks.
candidates.impact: Stored XSS in the wiki origin: script executes for any user viewing the affected page's info/history (including administrators), enabling session/CSRF-token theft, forced actions as the victim, and potentially administrator account takeover. The reflected variant compromises the editing user's own session via the preview page.
candidates.prerequisites: A user with page edit/comment permission (default deployments grant edit to the Authenticated role; anonymous editing is possible in permissive policies). Victim/observer must render the affected content: the page's Info tab (PageInfo.jsp -> InfoContent.jsp) for the stored variant, or an editor/preview view that re-displays the session change note for the reflected variant. No admin privileges required.
candidates.root_cause: Edit.jsp reads the 'changenote' HTTP parameter without applying TextUtil.replaceEntities() (line 73), unlike Comment.jsp (line 86) and AttachmentServlet (line 521) which DO escape it. The raw value is attached to the page as WikiPage.CHANGENOTE (lines 163-170) and also stored in the session on preview/redirect (line 247). The value is persisted verbatim by the page providers (e.g. VersioningFileProvider.java lines 519-523 / 618-619) and later rendered without output encoding by the templates: templates/default/InfoContent.jsp line 207 ('${changenote}' in HTML body, no fn:escapeXml/c:out), templates/210/InfoContent.jsp lines 246-248 and 398-400 (raw scriptlet '<%= changenote %>'), and the editors put it unescaped into an attribute value (templates/default/editors/plain.jsp lines 111-113, templates/210/editors/plain.jsp line 124, preview.jsp line 54).
candidates.title: Stored/reflected XSS via unescaped change note (Edit.jsp -> page attribute -> Info/editor templates)
candidates.trace: 1) POST Edit.jsp?page=X with text and changenote=<script>...</script> (or, for the reflection variant, changenote="><script>...</script> plus preview). 2) Edit.jsp:73 reads it unescaped; 163-169 stores it as modifiedPage.setAttribute(WikiPage.CHANGENOTE, changenote); 247 also puts it in the session on preview. 3) WikiEngine.saveText -> PreSaveWikiPageTask -> SaveWikiPageTask.java:55-58 calls PageManager.putPageText(page, text) with that same page object. 4) Provider persists the raw value (VersioningFileProvider.java:519-523 writes '<version>.changenote'; read back at 618-619, FileSystemProvider 87-90/136-140 similarly). 5) Any later view of PageInfo.jsp for that page renders each version through templates/default/InfoContent.jsp:206-207 (${changenote}) or templates/210/InfoContent.jsp:247-248 (<%= changenote %>) directly into the HTML body, executing attacker script in the wiki origin. 6) On preview/redirect the same unescaped session value is written into value="${changenote}" inputs in the editor templates, allowing attribute breakout reflection.
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution or servlet-container rendering was performed; JSP EL/scriptlet escaping behavior is asserted from the source (standard JSP semantics, no c:out/fn:escapeXml on these values). The effective edit/comment permission defaults live in jspwiki.policy, which is not present in this snapshot. Whether upstream M4 also lacked this escaping (i.e. whether this is an upstream bug or a modified file) could not be checked without external references; the internal inconsistency with Comment.jsp/AttachmentServlet is the main evidence.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') - stored XSS

coverage_summary: Read the scope report (1158 model-visible files; binary-like files skipped; no symlink/sensitive-name exclusions). Inspected the main request-handling and security-relevant areas: Edit/Comment/PageInfo/Group/Login/Attachment/Admin JSPs and templates (default and 210), AttachmentServlet, WikiAjaxDispatcherServlet/JSON modules, XML-RPC and Atom servlets, UserManager/GroupManager/AuthorizationManager/JAAS login modules, ACL/group/permission classes, page and attachment providers, JSPWikiMarkupParser/LinkParser/LinkParsingOperations, TemplateManager/WikiContext/WikiEngine, RenderingManager/WysiwygEditingRenderer, Preferences, Serializer and file utilities. Also searched for exec/deserialization/SQL/redirect/file-write sinks and for request-parameter use across Java and JSP sources. Full text of every one of the 1158 files was not read; prioritization was risk-based.
limitations: No tests are present in the snapshot and no code/tests/scanners were executed; conclusions are source-level only and not runtime-confirmed.
WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy (default permission grants) is absent, so effective edit/comment/createGroups permissions for anonymous/Authenticated users could not be verified from the snapshot.
JSP EL and scriptlet escaping behavior is inferred from standard JSP semantics; the exact rendered output was not observed.

Upstream/diff data, advisories and patch history were not consulted (prohibited), so it is not possible to state whether the missing escaping in Edit.jsp is an upstream defect or a modified line; the evidence is the internal inconsistency with Comment.jsp/AttachmentServlet and the unescaped sinks.
Binary-like and excluded files were not inspected per the scope report.

rejected_leads.lead: WikiContext.setDefaultTemplate (WikiContext.java:813-844) takes the request 'skin' parameter with no validation and feeds TemplateManager.findResource/makeFullJSPName ('/templates/'+template+'/'+name) and pageContext.include.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable, but a successful traversal must land on a file with the exact template name requested (ViewTemplate.jsp/PageContent.jsp/...). Requested names are constants and directories containing those names could not be identified; impact beyond template selection is unconfirmed. Also WikiEngine.enforceValidTemplateDirectory only validates the configured template.

rejected_leads.lead: Group.RESTRICTED_GROUPNAMES (Group.java:63-64) omits 'Admin', while the docs say groups cannot share a built-in role name and the default security policy reportedly grants AllPermission to the Admin wiki group; a user with createGroups might create/join an Admin-named group.
rejected_leads.reason: Contradicted by installer behavior in this snapshot: Installer.createAdministrator (Installer.java:150-162) relies on GroupManager.parseGroup(ADMIN_GROUP, ADMIN_NAME, true) succeeding, so 'Admin' must be creatable in upstream as well; NewGroup.jsp also refuses to overwrite an existing group, and the policy file that would grant the privilege is not in the snapshot. Left unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: SampleAjaxPlugin.service (SampleAjaxPlugin.java:55-60) echoes the request-provided actionName/params into the response without escaping.
rejected_leads.reason: The class is not registered with WikiAjaxDispatcherServlet anywhere in the snapshot (no registerServlet call/alias for it), so the endpoint is not reachable by default.

rejected_leads.lead: Serializer.deserializeFromBase64 (jspwiki-util Serializer.java:60-71) performs Java deserialization of user-profile attributes in XMLUserDatabase:685 / JDBCUserDatabase:744.
rejected_leads.reason: No web-reachable path that writes attacker-chosen serialized attribute values was found in this snapshot; stored data is plugin/admin-supplied. Attacker control not established.

rejected_leads.lead: templates/default/PageTab.jsp:49 and other templates echo ${param.page} / ${param.tab} unescaped.
rejected_leads.reason: The old-version branch requires an existing page whose name contains quote/angle characters; page-name sanitization along CommandResolver/MarkupParser.wikifyLink was not fully traced and no concrete payload/named page was demonstrated. Lower confidence than the change-note issue.
Command string comes from jspwiki.diffCommand configuration (admin-controlled), not from request input; temp file paths, not user strings, are substituted.

summary: Review of the JSPWiki 2.11.0.M4 snapshot (1158 visible files, no test sources, no jspwiki.policy) focused on request handling, auth, providers, parser/renderers and JSP templates. One candidate submitted: an unescaped change note flows from the edit request into a persisted page attribute and is emitted as raw HTML by the Info/editor templates (stored XSS). Other leads (skin template traversal, group-name/Admin, SampleAjaxPlugin echo, profile-attribute Java deserialization, PageTab param reflection) were examined and rejected or left unconfirmed as noted.
